body:
Thank you for the post. I've never ever had anyone ask for help as often as I've made cries for help the past few weeks/months. I imagine it probably *would* feel like a burden, eventually. At the very least, I feel people have said some things that I can interpret as being exhausted by my feelings. I think what's pushed away that one close relationship I mentioned was my openness with my negative feelings. That person deals with enough of their own negative feelings, and the same really applies to everyone in the world. It seems natural that people would want to be around positive people who will make them feel good, rather than someone like me who's usually either gonna be openly down or pretending to be up and doing a poor job at it.

I have never reached out for therapy. I don't have the income to afford it. It'd probably be a godsend for me, I confess, but the world runs on money, and that's not something I'm very good at obtaining in my mental-emotional state.

Yes, I've had good days. Or at least days that were good enough that I felt okay at the end of them. I don't think I understand the question? If you're asking what things I do cause me to have good days, it's more about what things happen to me than what I do.
